name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,475

clue.text: To die from contents of hamper is horrendous

indicators.note: the contents of something are what lies inside it, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gaps between these three words

explanation.surface: Someone dies after eating the dreadful food packed in a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to lose one's life, especially through violence, privation or accident.

clue.text: Original reward for victory said to include money

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the spelling may change while the sound stays
to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a prize is won; prise (to lever open) is pronounced the same
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A spoken boast that a winner's prize includes cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' applies only to the reward: the word that sounds like it is spelt differently, meaning to lever open.
explanation.definitionFit: Pristine describes something in its first, unspoilt state, just as original things are untouched by later change.

clue.text: Ponder upon team in trouble after game

indicators.note: words in trouble are thrown into disorder, so their letters get rearranged

blocks.note: RU is rugby union, the usual crossword game
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A manager broods over a side struggling after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after game' puts RU first, since the rearranged letters come after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruminate is to turn a matter over slowly and deeply in the mind, like a cow chewing cud.

clue.text: Locate it in the middle of Ossett

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central pair of letters, discarding the rest
one piece placed in another is put inside it

blocks.note: the central two of six letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to place something at the heart of a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossett is a small town in West Yorkshire; only its middle two letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to position or locate it in a particular place, as with a building.

clue.text: Indignant when Dicky ruins map

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so these letters are out of working order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone is cross because a man called Dicky has spoiled the map.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name, but it is the British adjective meaning shaky or faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in arms is an idiom for protesting angrily, so it matches feeling indignant.

clue.text: Caught out of school with hippies struggling to reason like Kant

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from it
struggling letters are wrestling about, so they end up in a new order

blocks.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
taken as written
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A pupil caught skipping school with hippies tries hard to think like a great philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C from SCHOOL to leave SHOOL, then rearrange it together with HIPPIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was a German philosopher, so reasoning in his manner is to philosophise, theorising about ideas.

clue.text: Growth of new type of poem

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
an ode is a lyric poem addressed to its subject

explanation.surface: A writer describes the rise of a fresh poetic form.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a node is a small swelling or lump, a kind of growth on the body.

clue.text: President from Georgia featured in article supporting soldiers

indicators.note: something featured in another appears within it
in a down entry a supporting piece sits beneath the one it holds up

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
an indefinite article
GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece backs troops and names a Georgian-born politician.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'supporting' means placed underneath, so the soldiers come first and the article goes below them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth holder of the top office in the United States, from 1981 to 1989.

clue.text: Note on West African country's language

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece on another sits on top of it

blocks.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
a landlocked nation in West Africa

explanation.surface: A comment about the national tongue of a country in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Mali's tongue, but the answer is the speech of an East African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Somali is the Cushitic tongue spoken in Somalia and neighbouring regions of the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Popular film about holding Massachusetts' fellow in prison

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the film's title runs backwards
holding something means keeping it inside

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film about an extraterrestrial
MA is the US postal abbreviation

explanation.surface: A hit movie about a jail breakout in Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: IN plus the reversed film TE together hold MA in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a person confined in an institution, especially a prisoner sharing a jail with others.

clue.text: Spooner's to come across kind-hearted energy supplier

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds trade places

blocks.note: to come across something is to find it; its opening sound is swapped with the next word's
a warm person is kind-hearted; it takes the other word's opening sound

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a generous power company.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of FIND WARM gives WIND FARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind farm is a group of turbines generating electricity, so it supplies power to the grid.

clue.text: Carry with difficulty from edge of motorway

blocks.note: hard can mean with great effort
to shoulder a load is to carry it

explanation.surface: Something heavy is dragged off the side of a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in the opposite order to the answer. A motorway is a British major highway.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard shoulder is the paved strip beside a British motorway where broken-down vehicles stop.

clue.text: Head over to Spain by air

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read the other way

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Instructions to fly over to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by air' looks like travel, but air is the definition: a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a simple melody or song, so it is another word for a tune.

clue.text: Is able to proceed with church decree

blocks.note: can means is able to
on as in go on, carry forward

explanation.surface: Someone may go ahead under a ruling from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a law or rule laid down by an ecclesiastical council, part of church law.

clue.text: Start to check everyone's name

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: its opening letter
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A roll call begins by checking the name of each person present.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to name them, as in calling a baby Jack.

clue.text: Freak out as Spanish-speaker's husband is taken away

indicators.note: pieces taken away are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: a Hispanic person is from a Spanish-speaking background
H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife is alarmed when her Latin American spouse is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip H and IS from the front of HISPANIC to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To panic is to be overcome by sudden fear, which is what freaking out means informally.

clue.text: Son died going after brown bear

indicators.note: going after means placed behind, fixing the order of the pieces

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
tan is a light brown colour
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A boy was killed by a brown bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown bear' reads as the animal, but bear is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate or endure it, the same as being able to stand it.

clue.text: The basic facts revealed by demented novelist and playwright found inside

indicators.note: found inside means placed within another word

blocks.note: nuts is slang for mad
George Sand was the French novelist
Robert Bolt wrote A Man for All Seasons

explanation.surface: A crazed writer of novels and plays gives away the fundamentals.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin; both writers sit inside the word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts and bolts is an idiom for the essential practical details of a subject, its fundamentals.

clue.text: A kind of merchant is how Cole introduced himself

blocks.note: a man introducing himself says I'm followed by his name
Cole Porter was the American songwriter

explanation.surface: A wry claim that a merchant's job is how a famous songwriter announced himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter would say "I'm Porter", which runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a trader who brings goods into a country from abroad to sell.

clue.text: Why tour rearranged to take in Norway is not acceptable

indicators.note: rearranged letters are put into a fresh order
to take something in is to admit it inside

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A complaint that a revised trip including Norway is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unworthy falls below the standard expected, so it is not acceptable or deserving.

clue.text: Round of applause after preferred fellow becomes chief assistant

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: the right hand is the preferred one for most people
give someone a big hand means applaud them
taken as a synonym

explanation.surface: Clapping greets a favoured man on his promotion to top aide.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a person's most trusted and indispensable helper, a principal deputy.

clue.text: Began to remove loose ends at first

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these two words
to doff a hat is to remove it

explanation.surface: Someone starts by trimming away stray threads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' governs loose ends, so those two initials precede DOFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to begin or open proceedings, so led off is the past tense of starting.

clue.text: Managed with what was available when appointed by Rob

blocks.note: made as in made captain, appointed
do is slang for cheat or rob

explanation.surface: Someone coped with limited means after being assigned by a man named Rob.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob looks like a name, but it is a verb, matched by the slang do.
explanation.definitionFit: Made do is an idiom for getting by with whatever limited resources were at hand.

clue.text: Vigour and style exhibited by the French in Parisian houses

indicators.note: a word that houses another holds it inside like a home

blocks.note: en is French for in
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: French homes display flair and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb for holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is energetic flair and confidence, borrowed from French, combining vigour with style.

clue.text: Tend to manage in recession with a couple of servants

indicators.note: something in recession is going backwards, so the word runs the other way
a couple means just two, the first pair of letters

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
its first two letters

explanation.surface: Running a household with only two staff during an economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse someone is to look after or care for them, the same as tending to them.

clue.text: Symbol for 'Gentlemen' primarily seen outside toilet? Just the opposite

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter is kept
seen outside means wrapped around the other piece; the clue then says to swap which goes round which

blocks.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sign for the men's room posted outside the toilets.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally G would go round LOO; 'Just the opposite' reverses that, so LOO goes round G.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or graphic mark used to identify a company, a kind of symbol.

clue.text: Conflict with Germany sent up in sketch

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a war is an armed conflict
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A war with Germany is satirised in a comedy sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' also means mocked, which suits the comic sketch of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw is to sketch a picture with pencil or pen, making lines on paper.

clue.text: Sheer power shown by river

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The raw force of a river in flood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer and pure both mean utter or absolute, as in sheer luck or pure chance.

clue.text: Foreign order I've set aside

indicators.note: foreign means strange and unfamiliar, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone has dismissed a command from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To override a decision is to overrule it, cancelling it and putting it aside.

clue.text: An exclamation of mild disapprobation whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: whichever way you look means the word reads identically from the front or from the back

blocks.clueFragment: whichever way you look at it
blocks.note: surface only: it says the answer is symmetrical

explanation.surface: A disapproving sound that stays the same from any angle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long opening phrase; the rest tells you the answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut-tut is the clicking sound people make to show they mildly disapprove of something.

clue.text: Skilful Manoeuvring's a book by a former Labour leader

indicators.note: by means written by, so the author's name stands beside the title

blocks.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
a work is a book or other piece of writing

explanation.surface: A political memoir by an old Labour leader about clever tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: The author's name comes first, ahead of the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwork is adroit movement of the feet, and figuratively nimble handling of a tricky situation.

clue.text: John's back in good time? Not quite

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: its final letter
arriving in good time means early

explanation.surface: John made it back punctually, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means almost but not completely, the same as not quite.
